text.p: Tanzania has expelled some 120 Burundian Hutu refugees accused of formenting trouble in camps in the northwest of the country, a U.N. refugee agency official said on Saturday.

Hitoshi Mise of the U.N. High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR) told Reuters the refugees were given orders on Saturday and had returned to their ethnically-divided central African state. Their fate was unknown.
Mise said the refugees were from Kitale camp in Tanzania, hit by factional fighting between Hutu groups since December. U.N. officials say more than 10 refugees had died in clashes.

Mise said the fighting pitted members of Palepehutu, a radical group of Hutus opposed to the Tutsi army junta in Burundi, against elements of the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD), a guerrilla group waging war against Burundi's army.
Mise said all the 120 expelled were members of the Palepehutu.

Tanzania is home to over 80,000 Burundian Hutu refugees who fled war in their tea and coffee-growing nation. Last month, the east African nation, a traditional haven for refugees in the strife-torn region, ordered more than 500,000 Rwandan refugees back home.

UNHCR officials say well over 400,000 Rwandans returned to the land they fled after civil war and genocidal killings in 1994. U.N. human rights officials say more than 2,000 have since been arrested for their role in the genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus.

Burundi has remained unstable since the 1993 murder of the country's first freely-elected president, Melchior Ndadaye, a Hutu. A civil war between Hutu guerrillas and the Tutsi-dominated army has cost at least 150,000 lives.
